provenance.description: Advisory scheduling hypothesis from measured setup/call/teardown records; not acceptance evidence or proof of the 300-second target. Latest successful node observations replace earlier observations; failed or unexecuted nodes retain their previous observation. The first three shared-fixture groups retain consumer call/teardown costs plus one maximum observed cold setup charge assigned to the first sorted consumer. The fourth serial/resource-affinity group retains both independent nodes full setup/call/teardown costs without normalization. Its proposed serialization addresses possible nested-worker contention; speed benefit is unmeasured. Failed nodes remain timing observations, never reusable test evidence.

group_sources.cost_policy: Full setup/call/teardown per node; no shared setup normalization.
group_sources.hypothesis: Serializing these two independent proofs may reduce overlapping nested-worker contention; no causal speedup is established.

prediction_limitations: Node durations vary with runner speed, co-location and worker concurrency.
The phase model excludes provisioning, worker startup, command overhead and cross-job launch skew.
No measured speedup is assumed for the fourth group; hosted execution and exact gates must establish acceptance.
